title: Littleness is not measured by the body
source_text: Πρὸς ταῦτα δὴ πυνθανόμεθα τῶν ἀποδεχομένων τὰ οὕτω καθ᾿ ἡμῶν εἰρημένα καί φαμεν· ἆρα πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὁρμαθὸν εἶναι νυκτερίδων ἢ μύρμηκας ἢ βατράχους ἢ σκώληκας ὑπολαμβάνετε διὰ τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ὑπεροχήν; ἢ τοὺς μὲν ἄλλους ἀνθρώπους εἰς τὴν προκειμένην εἰκόνα μὴ παραλαμβάνετε ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸ λογικὸν καὶ τοὺς καθεστῶτας νόμους τηρεῖτε αὐτοὺς ἀνθρώπους. Χριστιανοὺς δὲ καὶ Ἰουδαίους διὰ τὰ μὴ ἀρέσκοντα ὑμῖν αὐτῶν δόγματα ἐξευτελίζοντες τούτοις τοῖς ζῴοις παραβεβλήκατε; καὶ ὁπότερόν γε ἂν εἴπητε πρὸς τὴν πεῦσιν ἡμῶν, ἀποκρινούμεθα ἀποδεικνύναι πειρώμενοι οὐ δεόντως λελέχθαι περὶ τῶν πάντων ἀνθρώπων ἢ περὶ ἡμῶν τὰ τοιαῦτα. ἔστω γὰρ ὑμᾶς πρῶτον λέγειν ὅτι πάντες ἄνθρωποι ὡς πρὸς θεὸν τοῖς εὐτελέσι τούτοις παραβάλλονται ζῴοις. ἐπεὶ μηδαμῶς ἐστιν αὐτῶν ἡ μικρότης συγκριτὴ τῇ ὑπεροχῇ τοῦ θεοῦ. ποία δὴ μικρότης; ἀποκρίνασθέ μοι, ὦ οὗτοι. εἰ μὲν γὰρ ἡ τῶν σωμάτων, ἀκούσατε ὅτι τὸ ὑπερέχον καὶ τὸ ἐνδέον ὡς πρὸς ἀλήθειαν δικάζουσαν οὐκ ἐν σώματι κρίνεται· οὕτω γὰρ γρῦπες καὶ ἐλέφαντες ἡμῶν τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἔσονται κρείττους, καὶ γὰρ μείζους καὶ ἰσχυρότεροι καὶ πολυχρονιώτεροι οὗτοι· ἀλλ᾿ οὐδεὶς ἂν τῶν εὖ φρονούντων λέγοι κρείττονα εἶναι διὰ τὰ σώματα τάδε τὰ ἄλογα τῶν λογικῶν (πολὺ γὰρ εἶς ὑπεροχὴν ἀνάγει ὁ λόγος τὸ λογικὸν παρὰ πάντα τὰ ἄλογα) ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ τὰ σπουδαῖα καὶ μακάρια, εἴτε, ὡς ὑμεῖς φατε, οἱ ἀγαθοὶ δαίμονες εἴτε. ὡς ἡμῖν ἔθος ὀνομάζειν. οἱ τοῦ θεοῦ ἄγγελοι ἢ αἱ ὁποιαιδηποτοῦν ὑπερέχουσαι τῶν ἀνθρώπων φύσεις· ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ τὸ ἐν αὐτοῖς λογικὸν τετελείωται καὶ κατὰ πᾶσαν ἀρετὴν πεποίωται.
pass_a_gloss: Against these things, then, we inquire (πυνθάνομαι) of those accepting (ἀποδέχομαι) the things said thus against us, and we say: do you suppose (ὑπολαμβάνω) all men (ἄνθρωποι) to be a cluster of bats or ants or frogs or worms because of the surpassing excellence (ὑπεροχή) of God? Or do you not take (παραλαμβάνω) the other men into the image set before (προκειμένη εἰκών), but because of the rational (τὸ λογικόν) and the established (καθεστῶτες) laws you keep (τηρέω) them men, whereas Christians and Jews, because of their doctrines not pleasing (ἀρέσκω) you, disparaging (ἐξευτελίζω) them, you have compared (παραβάλλω) to these animals (ζῷα)? And whichever (ὁπότερον) you say to our question (πεῦσις), we shall answer, trying to show that such things have not been said as is due (δεόντως) about all men or about us. For let it be (ἔστω) that you say first that all men, as in relation to God (ὡς πρὸς θεόν), are compared to these mean (εὐτελῆ) animals, since their smallness (μικρότης) is in no way comparable (συγκριτή) to the surpassing excellence of God. What sort of smallness, then? Answer me, you (ὦ οὗτοι). For if that of bodies (σώματα), hear that the surpassing (τὸ ὑπερέχον) and the falling short (τὸ ἐνδέον), with respect to truth judging (ἀλήθεια δικάζουσα), is not judged (κρίνω) in body; for thus griffins (γρῦπες) and elephants will be better (κρείττους) than us men, for these are larger and stronger and longer-lived (πολυχρονιώτεροι); but none of those thinking well (εὖ φρονέω) would say that these irrational ones (ἄλογα) are better than the rational ones (λογικά) because of their bodies (for reason (λόγος) leads up (ἀνάγω) the rational much into surpassing excellence beyond all the irrational), but neither the virtuous/excellent (σπουδαῖα) and blessed (μακάρια) ones, whether, as you say, the good daemons (ἀγαθοὶ δαίμονες), or, as is customary (ἔθος) for us to name, the angels (ἄγγελοι) of God, or the natures (φύσεις) of whatever kind (ὁποιαιδηποτοῦν) surpassing men; but since the rational in them has been perfected (τελειόω) and qualified/formed (ποιόω) according to all virtue (ἀρετή).
pass_b_english: In reply to this we ask those who accept what has been said against us in this way, and we say: Do you suppose that all human beings are a cluster of bats, or ants, or frogs, or worms, because of God’s surpassing greatness? Or do you leave the rest of humankind out of the picture set before us, and because of their reason and their established laws keep them as human beings, while you belittle Christians and Jews because of their doctrines, which do not please you, and so have compared them to these animals?

Whichever answer you give to our question, we shall reply by trying to show that such things have not been rightly said, whether of all human beings or of us. Suppose, first, you say that all human beings, in relation to God, are compared with these mean animals, since their littleness can in no way be compared with God’s surpassing greatness. What littleness do you mean? Answer me, you there.

If you mean the littleness of their bodies, hear this: when truth is the judge, what surpasses and what falls short is not decided by the body. For on that reckoning griffins and elephants will be better than us human beings, since they are larger and stronger and longer-lived than we are. Yet no one of sound mind would say that these irrational creatures are better than rational beings because of their bodies (for reason raises the rational being far above all irrational ones). Nor would he say that the virtuous and blessed beings are better because of their bodies, whether these are, as you say, the good demons, or, as we are accustomed to call them, the angels of God, or whatever natures there may be that surpass human beings; he would say they are better because the reason in them has been brought to perfection and formed in every virtue.

choices.choice: 'are to be compared' to 'are compared with' (present indicative παραβάλλονται, no modality)
'Answer me, sirs' to 'Answer me, you there' (ὦ οὗτοι; 'sirs' read as archaic)
elliptical last clause spelled out: the virtuous and blessed beings are not better 'because of their bodies' but because their reason is perfected (the old 'Nor would he say it of' left 'it' unclear)

'τηρεῖτε αὐτοὺς ἀνθρώπους' rendered 'keep them as human beings'. 'εἰς τὴν προκειμένην εἰκόνα' rendered 'in the picture set before us' (Celsus's comparison). παραβάλλονται is present indicative, rendered 'are compared with', not 'are to be compared'. ὦ οὗτοι is a brusque address, rendered 'you there'. γρῦπες are griffins (LSJ), creatures some ancients counted real; kept as 'griffins'. The parenthesis on reason keeps Origen's play on λόγος / λογικόν / ἄλογα. The final clause is elliptical: 'κρείττονα εἶναι διὰ τὰ σώματα' from the previous clause is understood with 'οὐδὲ τὰ σπουδαῖα καὶ μακάρια', and 'ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ' gives the true reason for their superiority; the English spells out the understood words ('are better because of their bodies', 'he would say they are better') without adding a new idea. δαίμονες rendered 'demons' as elsewhere in this translation; the qualifier 'good' and 'as you say' mark it as the Greek usage, set against the Christian name 'angels of God'. No Scripture quoted or clearly alluded to.
